design: A is on the LEFT: one visibly L-shaped two-storey building, two joined perpendicular wings around a deep open notch facing the center. The footprint and roof outline both unmistakably read as the Korean ㄱ / L shape. Use a shared continuous ochre plaster/painted-metal facade, recessed corner entrance, broad strip windows, one projecting bay and shallow rounded upper corners. Give the two wings different roof details: a long supported louvered service monitor and an offset repair canopy, with a visible unoccupied roof margin. Ground edges stay readable; do not fill the L notch with a separate shed. B is on the RIGHT: a one-storey maintenance/service building with a grounded human door, carrying a full SECOND-STOREY mechanical superstructure. Above the first-floor roof slab are two enormous reclaimed curved compressor/actuator housings, service manifolds and a visible supporting steel frame, nearly the size of an upper floor. No upper dwelling, room, window facade or ordinary enclosed second-storey house. Its mechanical volume shapes the building silhouette. A car is parked along the near-left edge, clear of the central road; a repaired utility pole stands at the rear between the buildings, with cables following the perimeter. The center is a dry, open asphalt street court with broad paving and a few painted lane remnants, coherent square curbs along the buildings. Front cut sections contain one large storm-water service pipe and a distinct electrical distribution bay, not the prior slum base design.
exits: LEFT transition: a broad CLOSED vertical roller shutter in A's rear wing, facing the central court, doubles as the rear-left route through the building. Keep its approach clear and its upward shutter travel free. The hidden onward passage continues toward the rear-left, no need to expose the interior. A's small domestic door is an ordinary non-transition entry. RIGHT transition: an OPEN street passage toward the rear-right edge, below/right of B, defined by B on one side and a low anchored utility enclosure on the other. Show clear paved ground all the way to this edge with no fence across it. Remaining rear gaps meet short solid industrial fences/utility housings. B's small door is ordinary, not another map exit.

roof_plan.A: louver monitor + supported repair canopy, about half each joined roof wing
roof_plan.B: entire upper level is mechanical; main housings and service deck about 65% of top floor slab

exit_states: closed roller shutter, rear-left through A
open road gap, rear-right beside B
correction_strategy: Two inputs only: new-scene guide controls geometry; same variant appearance is remapped. Remove external camera-bearing source images from correction.
